digest.en: The ICC rejected U.S. sanctions, declaring that history will judge this moment. Guterres condemned the move, highlighting a sharp fracture in multilateral diplomacy. Meanwhile, Yemen has fallen back into full-scale war, complicating regional stability efforts.
digest.hi: आज पाकिस्तान के कश्मीर में जैश कमांडर के आदेश पर किश्तवाड़ में एक साजिशी आतंकी हमला तैयार किया गया, जिसमें कई स्थानीय मिलिशिया शामिल थे।

articles.title: ICC rejects U.S. sanctions, says 'history will judge this moment'
articles.summary: The International Criminal Court rejected new United States sanctions, calling them an assault on the rule of law. The court stated that no one stands above the law. It added that history will judge this moment. The statement emphasized the foundations of the international legal order. The sanctions are "an assault on the rule of law and on the very foundations of the international legal order which strikes at the simple principle that no one stands above the law", said the court in a statement.

articles.title: Why A Starlink Test In Italy Has Iran's Internet Censors Worried
articles.summary: A Starlink trial in Italy connected a smartphone to the internet without mobile coverage or external antennas. The test drew attention in Iran. Iranian authorities heavily filter internet access. They imposed a near-total blackout during the January protests. A Starlink trial on an Italian hilltop connected an ordinary smartphone to the Internet without mobile coverage, a satellite dish, or an external antenna.

articles.title: Guterres condemns new US sanctions on International Criminal Court
articles.summary: The United States imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court as an institution. Secretary of State Marco Rubio vowed to dismantle the court unless it ends threats to American citizens. The move targets the court directly. Washington views its operations as a national security risk. The United States has imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) as an institution, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio vowing on Friday to “dismantle the ICC, brick by brick” unless it ends what Washington regards as a “threat” to its citizens.

articles.title: Amid heartache of Nepal flooding disaster, fear remains
articles.summary: Six weeks after Nepal’s deadly flooding, communities are still rebuilding. UNICEF warned that sustained help is needed. Global warming increases the risk of another Himalayan catastrophe. The disaster has left lasting impacts on local populations. Amid heartache of Nepal flooding disaster, fear remains.

articles.title: Yemen has fallen back into full-scale war, warns UN envoy
articles.summary: A UN envoy warned that Yemen has fallen back into full-scale war. A Houthi offensive launched in September escalated the twelve-year conflict. Spillover from the US-Iran war provoked a new displacement crisis. The Security Council met to discuss the worsening situation. The Security Council met to discuss the crisis in Yemen Friday, where a Houthi offensive launched in September has sharply escalated the 12-year-long war for control of the country and spillover from the US-Iran war has provoked a new displacement crisis.

articles.title: Afghans Desperate To Escape Poverty Sell Kidneys To Survive
articles.summary: Millions of Afghans struggle to afford basic food. Some have turned to selling a healthy kidney to survive. The financial gain is often modest and fails to clear family debts. One woman reported her health deteriorated significantly after the procedure. As millions of Afghans struggle just to afford food, some have turned to selling one of their last remaining resources: a healthy kidney.

articles.title: Too Soon? Swathes Of Chernobyl-Affected Land In Belarus To Lose 'Contaminated' Status
articles.summary: Belarus will remove contaminated status from 177 cities and towns on January 1, 2027. This change affects 566,400 people. The land was contaminated by the 1986 nuclear accident in Soviet Ukraine. A total of 930,600 people live in the affected territory. A recent announcement that 177 cities, towns and villages will lose their “contaminated” status on January 1, 2027 affects some 566,400 people from a total of 930,600 living on Belarusian territory that was contaminated by the 1986 nuclear accident in Soviet Ukraine.

articles.title: How a plant selfie in Colombian jungle led to ‘jaw dropping’ giant waterlily find
articles.summary: A social media post featuring a plant selfie in the Colombian jungle led to the discovery of a new giant waterlily species. The plant is so large it is visible from space but is already critically endangered. Conservationists are now working to protect the newly identified species in its natural habitat. Species with leaves large enough to be seen from space is already critically endangered – and plans are afoot to protect itA chance social media encounter has led to the race-against-time discovery of a new species of giant waterlily that has until now been hidden in the depths of Colombia’s jungle. But the plant, which is so huge it is visible from space, is already considered critically endangere.

articles.title: Healthcare needs outstrip resources as Security Council extends Sudan sanctions
articles.summary: The UN World Health Organization warned that over 700,000 displaced people in Tawila, Darfur, face severe shortages. They lack adequate healthcare, food, water, and protection. The agency called for an urgent increase in resources. The Security Council simultaneously extended sanctions on Sudan. More than 700,000 displaced people in Tawila, in Sudan’s war-ravaged Darfur region, face severe shortages of healthcare, food, water and protection, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Thursday as it called for an urgent increase in resources.

articles.title: ‘Age must never diminish rights,’ UN independent expert warns
articles.summary: A UN independent expert warned that older women face violence and neglect while remaining invisible in protective laws and policies. The report highlighted how existing frameworks fail to address the specific vulnerabilities of aging women globally. Older women around the world face violence, exploitation and neglect, yet remain largely invisible in the laws, policies, data and services designed to protect women overall, a UN independent human rights expert said on Thursday.

articles.title: Poverty deepens as families face multiple shocks with limited resources
articles.summary: The UN Development Programme reported that Myanmar is experiencing a simultaneous collapse of shelter, healthcare, and livelihoods. Years of conflict, displacement, and climate shocks have deepened poverty for millions of families with limited resources. Years of conflict, displacement, economic disruption and climate shocks in Myanmar have led to the “simultaneous collapse” of shelter, healthcare, schooling and livelihoods affecting millions of people, the UN Development Programme (UNDP) said in a report issued on Thursday.

articles.title: India’s Central Asia missile sales spark a new Great Game
articles.summary: India exported Akash missile systems to Tajikistan and Turkmenistan. Defense Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh confirmed the deals. Central Asian states seek alternative suppliers. This move counters Russia's waning dominance. It also addresses Sino-Indian rivalry. A flurry of landmark arms deals is reshaping Central Asia’s strategic landscape, as regional states leverage alternative defense suppliers to assert their sovereignty amid Russia’s waning dominance and an intensifying Sino-Indian rivalry.

articles.title: Bit by bit, the Taliban is losing control of Afghanistan
articles.summary: Armed resistance in Afghanistan is spreading beyond isolated pockets, challenging the Taliban's claim of stable governance. Five years after taking Kabul, the group still controls all provincial capitals. However, the growing geographic dispersion of insurgent groups undermines their argument for international acceptance. Five years after seizing Kabul, the Taliban’s strongest argument for international acceptance rests on control. The Taliban governs every provincial capital and faces no conventional army capable of marching on Kabul.

articles.title: Exiled Russian Activist Describes How Kremlin Targets Critics Abroad
articles.summary: Mikhail Klimaryov, a Russian activist living in Germany, says Kremlin agents continue to target him abroad. The persistent pressure has driven him into a state of paranoia regarding his personal safety. He fled Russia to escape political persecution but remains under constant surveillance. Mikhail Klimaryov fled Russia to escape political persecution and now lives in Germany, but says he is still not safe.

articles.title: Kenya races to trace all contacts after first Ebola death, WHO official says
articles.summary: Kenya is tracing all contacts of its first Ebola death case. The World Health Organization’s top official in the country confirmed that the United Nations and partners are providing full support for the rapid response effort. Kenya’s first Ebola death has triggered a race to trace everyone the victim came into contact with, as the United Nations and partners provide full support, the World Health Organization’s (WHO) top official in the country has told UN News in her first interview on the case.

articles.title: On Our Radar
articles.summary: Crisis Group’s On Our Radar scans global conflicts and crises weekly. Field experts highlight under-reported trends and major developments. They explain why specific hotspots matter. The brief outlines what actions are needed to address these ongoing situations. On Our Radar scans conflicts and crises around the globe every week and features some of the hotspots Crisis Group’s analysts are closely watching.

articles.title: Five Energy Market Factors That Could Tip the Scales in the Middle East War
articles.summary: Washington and Tehran are fighting over global energy prices, with the United States seeking lower costs and Iran aiming to keep them high. Five specific market developments will determine whether the conflict escalates or de-escalates. The outcome hinges on how these factors shift fuel and gas pricing dynamics. Oil, gas and fuel prices are central to the U. S.-Israeli war with Iran, with Washington striving to lower them and Tehran to keep them high.

articles.title: Inside Sudan’s War
articles.summary: Sky News Africa correspondent Yousra Elbagir discussed her reporting from inside Sudan’s ongoing war on The Horn podcast. She detailed conditions in El Obeid and El Fasher, describing how civilians are surviving the conflict. The conversation also explored potential pathways for ending the war. In this episode of The Horn, Alan speaks with Yousra Elbagir, Sky News’s Africa correspondent, about her reporting from inside Sudan’s war, including around El Obeid and El Fasher, how Sudanese are surviving the war and how the war could end.

articles.title: Back to War in Ethiopia?
articles.summary: Crisis Group Africa director Murithi Mutiga told Hold Your Fire! that fighting has resumed in Ethiopia’s northern Tigray region, raising the risk of spillover into Sudan and Eritrea. He warned that renewed clashes could push the dispute toward full‑scale war and strain ongoing diplomatic initiatives This week on Hold Your Fire!, Richard speaks with Crisis Group’s Africa director Murithi Mutiga about renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia, how the conflict could unfold, the risks of regional escalation and whether diplomacy can still stop the slide into all-out war.

articles.title: पाकिस्तान में रची गई थी किश्तवाड़ आतंकी हमले की साजिश, जैश कमांडर दे रहा था हुक्म
articles.summary: राष्ट्रीय जांच एजेंसी ने किश्तवाड़ आतंकी हमले से जुड़ा 535 पन्ने का आरोपपत्र दाखिल किया। एनआईए का दावा है कि साजिश पाकिस्तान में रची गई थी। जैश कमांडर ने हमले के लिए हुक्म दिया था। किश्तवाड़ के छत्रू क्षेत्र में हुए आतंकी हमले की साजिश पाकिस्तान में रचे जाने का उल्लेख करते हुए राष्ट्रीय जांच एजेंसी (एनआईए) ने शुक्रवार को 535 पन्नों का आरोपपत्र दाखिल किया है।

articles.title: वियतनाम में मिला तेल-गैस का खजाना, लूटने को दौड़ पड़े अमेरिका-जापान और रूस, शैतान बच्चों वाली हरकत
articles.summary: वियतनाम साउथ चाइना सी में तेल और गैस खोजने की रफ्तार बढ़ा रहा है। देश महंगे विदेशी ईंधन पर निर्भरता घटाना चाहता है। अमेरिका, जापान और रूस की कंपनियों को न्योता दिया गया है। पश्चिम एशिया में जंग और होर्मुज संकट की वजह से दुनियाभर में तेल-गैस के दाम आसमान छू रहे हैं. ऐसे माहौल में वियतनाम ने साउथ चाइना सी में छिपे अपने तेल और गैस के खजाने को तेजी से निकालना शुरू कर दिया है.

articles.summary: नावी पिल्लई ने नोबेल पुरस्कार के बाद मीडिया से बातचीत की। उन्होंने डोनाल्ड ट्रंप पर तंज कसा। पिल्लई ने कहा कि अगर लोग ज़्यादा तालियां बजाएंगे तो वह पुरस्कार ट्रंप के साथ बांट देंगी। 'नोबेल शांति पुरस्कार' का ऐलान होने के बाद नावी पिल्लई एक प्रोग्राम के दौरान पहली बार मीडिया के सामने आईं. आते ही उन्होंने अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रंप पर तंज कस डाला.

articles.summary: यमन के हूती विद्रोहियों ने ईरान के निर्देश पर सऊदी अरब के नागरिक ठिकानों पर हमले शुरू कर दिए हैं। पहले वे केवल सैन्य लक्ष्यों को निशाना बनाते थे। अब रियाद इंटरनेशनल एयरपोर्ट जैसी नागरिक संस्थाओं पर भी हमले हो रहे हैं। यमन की सरकारी सेना सऊदी के समर्थन में हूतियों के खिलाफ सैन्य कार्रवाई कर रही है। यमन (Yemen) के हूती विद्रोहियों (Houthis) और सऊदी अरब (Saudi Arabia) के बीच तनाव ने अब ऐसा रूप ले लिया है जैसे जंग छिड़ गई हो।

articles.summary: दक्षिण अफ्रीका के डरबन में जन्मीं नावी पिल्लई को 2026 का नोबेल शांति पुरस्कार मिला। उन्होंने रंगभेद के खिलाफ कानूनी बचाव किया और संयुक्त राष्ट्र में मानवाधिकारों की रक्षा की। वह दक्षिण अफ्रीका की पहली अश्वेत महिला हाईकोर्ट जज भी रहीं। Nobel Peace Prize 2026: नेल्सन मंडेला के दौर में रंगभेद के खिलाफ आवाज उठाने वालों का कानूनी बचाव करने से लेकर संयुक्त राष्ट्र में मानवाधिकारों की रक्षा तक, नावी पिल्लई का सफर कई अहम पड़ावों से होकर गुजरा है.

articles.title: ट्रक से भीषण टक्कर के बाद बस में लगी आग, तंज़ानिया में 28 लोगों की मौत
articles.summary: तंज़ानिया के मोरोगोरो जिले में 9 अक्टूबर को बस और ट्रक की भिड़ंत हुई। टक्कर के बाद बस में आग लग गई। इस हादसे में 28 लोगों की मौत हो गई। दुनियाभर में अक्सर ही रोड एक्सीडेंट्स (Road Accidents) के कई मामले देखने को मिलते हैं। रोड सेफ्टी को वैसे तो हर देश में बेहद ही अहम माना जाता है, पर अक्सर ही इसमें चूक होने से रोड एक्सीडेंट्स के मामले सामने आते हैं।
